verses.text: Brothers and sisters, what I want most, and what I pray to God for, is that Israel would be saved.
I can testify about them: they have a real passion for God, but it isn't guided by understanding.
They don't understand God's way of making people right. Trying to establish their own, they haven't submitted to God's righteousness.
Christ is the goal of the law, so that everyone who believes can be made right with God.
Moses writes about righteousness through the law: ‘The person who does these things will live by them.’
But righteousness through faith says: ‘Don't say in your heart, Who will go up to heaven?’ (That would be to bring Christ down.)
‘Or ask, Who will go down into the abyss?’ (That would be to bring Christ up from the dead.)
But what does it say? ‘The message is near you—in your mouth and in your heart.’ That's the message of faith we're preaching:
If you declare with your mouth, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
With the heart a person believes and is made right with God; with the mouth a person declares faith and is saved.
Scripture says, ‘Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.’
There is no difference between Jew and Greek. The same Lord is Lord of everyone and richly blesses all who call on him.
For Scripture says, ‘Everyone who calls on the Lord's name will be saved.’
But how can people call on someone they haven't believed in? How can they believe in someone they haven't heard about? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them?
And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As Scripture says, ‘How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the Good News!’
But not everyone welcomed the Good News. Isaiah says, ‘Lord, who believed what we announced?’
So faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.
But I ask: Didn't they hear? Of course they did: ‘Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.’
But I ask: Didn't Israel understand? First, Moses says, ‘I will make you jealous of those who are not a nation; I will make you angry through a people without understanding.’
Then Isaiah speaks boldly: ‘I was found by those who weren't looking for me. I showed myself to those who weren't asking for me.’
But about Israel he says, ‘All day long I held out my hands to a disobedient and stubborn people.’
